title: Tool Lending Desk
summary: A tool library needs one record for each model it lends.

levels.title: Tool Catalog
levels.requirements:
Three bench planes came in with a donation. At the desk, staff need to add them to the catalog, correct a count after a stocktake, and remove a model they no longer carry.

A new LendingDesk has an empty catalog. Each tool ID identifies a model, such as plane. Each record has a category and a positive integer count of copies in the catalog. IDs and categories are non-empty ASCII strings. Compare them exactly as written.

add_tool(tool_id, category, units) adds a record and returns True. Return False if the ID already exists or units is zero or negative.

get_tool(tool_id) returns a new [category, units] list for an existing ID. Return None if the ID is missing.

update_tool(tool_id, category, units) replaces both fields of an existing record and returns True. Return False if the ID is missing or units is zero or negative. An update to the same values still succeeds.

remove_tool(tool_id) removes an existing record and returns True. Return False if the ID is missing. A removed ID can be added again.

A failed operation leaves the catalog unchanged. The tests only pass arguments of the stated types.

questions.prompt: What must be true before the tool can change?
choices: The tool ID must exist and units must be greater than zero.
Units can be zero if the tool already exists.

questions.prompt: Which fields does a successful update replace?
What does an update return when the tool ID is missing?
What happens if both new values equal the current values?
choices: The update succeeds and returns True.

levels.title: Stock Summaries
levels.requirements:
Before the next stocktake, staff want a count for each shelf category and a short list of models with the most copies. Read the current catalog records. These counts include copies that can be out on loan. These methods leave the catalog unchanged.

total_units(category) returns the sum of stock counts for all current tools in that category. Return 0 if the category has no tools.

top_tools(limit) takes an integer and returns up to limit current tool IDs across all categories. Sort by stock count from largest to smallest. For equal stock counts, sort by ID from smallest to largest using case-sensitive string order. If limit is zero or negative, return an empty list. If the catalog contains fewer than limit records, return all current tool IDs in that order.

questions.prompt: What does the method do with a negative limit?
What changes in the catalog when the method ranks tools?
choices: It removes records outside the limit.

questions.prompt: What does the returned list contain?
If A and B have the same stock count, which ID comes first?

levels.title: Scheduled Holds
levels.requirements:
Staff keep a list of pickup reminders. When someone asks about a saw, staff can set a reminder to follow up later. Checkout happens in a separate system. These records do not reserve a copy or change stock. More than one person can have a reminder for the same model.

The method names call each reminder a hold. A hold has a unique hold ID and belongs to one tool model. Hold IDs are non-empty ASCII strings. Compare them exactly as written. A hold is active from its start time up to, but excluding, start + ttl. For example, a hold that starts at tick 5 with a ttl of 2 is active at ticks 5 and 6. It expires at tick 7.

All time arguments are integers. Calls that take now always pass a non-negative value greater than or equal to the previous now. Calls at the same time take effect in call order.

schedule_hold(hold_id, tool_id, start, ttl, now) records a hold and returns True. Return False if the tool does not exist, the hold ID was used in any successful schedule, start is less than now, or ttl is zero or negative. A failed schedule does not use the hold ID.

cancel_hold(hold_id, now) cancels a scheduled or active hold and returns True. Return False if the hold does not exist, is already cancelled, has reached its expiry time, or belongs to a tool that was removed. A cancelled hold ID remains used.

active_holds(tool_id, now) returns the active hold IDs for that tool in case-sensitive ascending string order. Return an empty list if there are none or if the tool does not exist.

Removing a tool cancels all its holds. Adding that tool ID again does not restore them. Updating a tool leaves its holds in place.

questions.prompt: When is a hold's start time valid?
choices: Only when start is greater than now.
Whenever start is zero or greater.
When start is greater than or equal to now.

questions.prompt: How does a successful schedule affect stock?
choices: It reduces the stock count by one.
The stock count stays the same.
It reduces the stock count when the hold becomes active.

questions.prompt: What does a schedule return after it records a valid hold?
A hold starts at 5 and has a TTL of 2. Is it active at time 7?
choices: Yes, time 7 is the last active time.
No, time 7 is the first expired time.

levels.title: Catalog History
levels.requirements:
A volunteer corrects the saw count at the end of the shift. The next volunteer needs to check what the catalog showed before that correction. Number the catalog changes so staff can look up earlier records.

The empty catalog is revision 0. Each successful add_tool, update_tool, or remove_tool operation advances the whole catalog revision by exactly one. This includes an update that writes the same values. Failed operations, reads, and all hold operations leave the revision unchanged.

revision() returns the current catalog revision as an integer.

tool_at(tool_id, revision) takes an integer revision and returns a new [category, units] list as the tool existed immediately after that revision. Return None if the revision is negative or greater than the current revision, or if the tool did not exist at that revision. Tool history persists when a tool is removed and when its ID is used again. Reading history does not change the current catalog.

questions.prompt: Which revision numbers are valid for a historical lookup?
choices: Revisions from 0 through the current revision, inclusive.

questions.prompt: What happens to the current catalog when you read a past revision?
choices: The current revision increases by one.

questions.prompt: What does tool_at return for a tool present at the requested revision?
A tool was removed at revision 3 and added again at revision 4. What does tool_at return for revision 3?
